claims.source_quote_ar: وَالْمَعْنَى يَتِمُّ بِدُخُولِ الْهَمْزَةِ عَلَى جُمْلَةِ الشَّرْطِ وَالْجَوَابِ
claims.claim_ar: الهمزة في «إِنْ» لها صدر الكلام، وبدخولها على جملة الشرط وجملة الجواب يتم المعنى؛ أي أن همزة الشرط تتعلق بكلتا الجملتين وتكمل المعنى.
claims.claim_en: The hamza of 'إِن' has a sadr (a vocal/intonational onset of the clause), and by the hamza entering both the protasis (conditional clause) and the apodosis (response) the meaning is completed; i.e., the hamza links and completes both parts of the conditional construction.

claims.source_quote_ar: الْهَمْزَةُ فِي مِثْلِ هَذَا حَقُّهَا أَنْ تَدْخُلَ عَلَى جَوَابِ الشَّرْطِ تَقْدِيرُهُ: أَتَنْقَلِبُونَ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ إِنْ مَاتَ
claims.claim_ar: في وجه من وجوه القراءة والإعراب، يجوز إدخال همزة الشرط على جواب الشرط بحيث يُقدَّر جواب مركب (أي يأخذ الهمز على نحو دخول الجواب)، فثمة قراءة/وجه يعامل الهمزة كأنها تدخل على الجواب.
claims.claim_en: According to a reading/grammatical opinion, it is permissible for the hamza of the conditional particle to enter the apodosis, so that the hamza is treated as part of the jawab; there is a qira'ah/analysis that attaches the hamza to the response.
claims.needs_review_reason: The cited discussion exemplifies this with constructions like أَفَإِنْ مَاتَ...; it should be verified whether this reading/analysis is explicitly applied to this specific ayah in transmission or is being analogically extended.

warnings: The provided source chunks discuss the behavior of the hamza and conditional constructions using examples (e.g., أَفَإِنْ مَاتَ...) from other verses; the claims above are drawn from those general discussions and applied to the word «وَإِنْ» in this ayah by analogy.

No explicit discussion of other words in the ayah (e.g., إِنَّمَا, الْحَيَاةُ, الدُّنْيَا, لَعِبٌ، لَهْوٌ, يُؤْتِكُمْ, أُجُورَكُمْ, يَسْأَلْكُمْ) was found in the supplied chunks, so no claims were made about them.
Some points in the source concern the role of the particle الفاء (fa') in constructions not present in this ayah; those remarks were not used to make claims for this verse.
